prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1049; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a collision at an intersection in which the insured's vehicle was struck while the other driver turned left across our insured's path. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reported a wrist injury and is currently driving the insured vehicle as a household member of the policyholder.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who described the crash the same way he did when first reported, saying the other vehicle turned in front of him as he proceeded through the intersection. His account has not changed in any conversation so far.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact and records the scene as consistent with a left-turn collision. Independent witnesses and the other driver give statements that match the claimant's version of events.

Entry 4: Collected scene photographs showing front-end damage to the insured vehicle and the side of the other vehicle. The photos are consistent with the reported impact, though I have not yet determined whether every area of damage resulted from this single event.

Entry 5: Requested the claimant's medical records. The reported wrist fracture is a plausible injury for a collision of this type, and no prior injury to that area appears in the file or was mentioned by the claimant.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a typical course, with the claimant attending scheduled follow-up visits and reporting steady improvement. Care has tapered as expected, and the treating provider's notes match that progression.

Entry 7: Confirmed with underwriting that no prior damage to the insured vehicle is on record and nothing indicates any damage predates the start of coverage on this policy.

Entry 8: Reviewed the repair estimate against the photos and the impact description. Some items on the estimate may not be explained by this collision alone, so I have asked the repair facility for a more detailed breakdown before settling those lines.

Entry 9: Verified that the claimant is a household member of the policyholder and therefore qualifies as a covered driver under the policy's terms. No exclusion applies based on the driver's relationship to the insured.

Entry 10: Coverage is confirmed for the collision and the claimant's injury. Remaining open items are the detailed repair breakdown and final medical billing. Reserves have been adjusted to reflect the current estimate, and the file will be reviewed again once those documents arrive.
